about.textOne: PTSD treatment is a medical approach to managing the long-term effects of trauma. Post-traumatic stress disorder is a serious mental health condition that develops after exposure to traumatic events such as violence, abuse, combat, or severe accidents. Symptoms include flashbacks, nightmares, hypervigilance, mood disturbances, and emotional numbness, often disrupting relationships, work, and daily life.
about.textTwo: At Clear Path in Orange County, PTSD treatment includes advanced psychopharmacological care tailored to each individual's history, symptoms, and recovery goals. Our in-person model allows for consistent oversight and access to innovative treatments like psychotherapy and psychotherapy for individuals who have not responded to standard medications. According to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, about 6% of adults in the United States will experience PTSD in their lifetime, and roughly 5% of adults live with PTSD in any given year.

hero.text: Clear Path is a leading behavioral health provider specializing in in-person psychiatric care for individuals living with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Focused on medication management and mental health intervention, our approach prioritizes direct, face-to-face care with board-certified psychiatrists and experienced psychiatric PAs.  We stand apart from telehealth-only providers by delivering evidence-based, in-office treatment designed to support healing from trauma with safety, structure, and clinical expertise.

video.heading: Why is PTSD Treatment
video.description: PTSD treatment is imperative to reduce the psychological and physical toll that trauma can have over time. Without intervention, PTSD increases the risk of co-occurring conditions like depression, substance use, and suicidal ideation. It can also impair memory, sleep, and emotional regulation, limiting a person's ability to function. Clear Path provides a safe, structured clinical setting where patients can address trauma through effective medical care. Our goal is to reduce the severity of symptoms, improve emotional resilience, and support long-term recovery with compassionate, in-person psychiatric support at our Orange County facility.
